translation_notes: six graph.add((s, p, o)) calls (three per nanopub) become six one-line `+= g{ ... }` islands; they are not merged further because each targets a different graph (np._assertion / np._provenance / np._pubinfo)

prefixes declared for the namespaces the region uses: nanopub.namespaces.HYCL -> hycl:, rdflib PROV -> prov:, rdflib DC -> dc:. The draft's rdf/dcterms/xsd prefixes are unused here and were dropped (they had also been spliced into the middle of a `from ... import (` statement, which does not parse)

URIRef("http://test") / URIRef("http://someone") -> <http://test> / <http://someone>; Literal("test claim") -> "test claim"; the computed terms np._assertion.identifier and np._metadata.namespace[""] stay {interpolations}

context (driver-side, identical for both representations): the nanopub package is not installed in the venv, so the corpus checkout Nanopublication/nanopub-py@05022dc4bc is put on sys.path before either module is executed

context shim: `from tests.conftest import ...` -> `from conftest_context import ...` (same names). Upstream conftest downloads the nanopub test suite at import time just to get the rsa-key1 pair and pings the nanopub server; the shim copies that key pair from Nanopublication/nanopub-testsuite@main (MIT) into the example directory and keeps the profile/NanopubConf definitions verbatim

the region returns nothing; its three pytest.raises blocks are the behavioural check, and they only hold if the three sub-graphs were populated identically (sign() rejects an empty/invalid nanopub with a different error)
